finding: The next_action precedence enumerates only three review branches (converged; convergence-blocking unresolved findings present; mechanize_candidates present) and two audit states (converged; non-converged = open non-PASS rows), but none covers the most common live-loop state: a round that is clean (no surviving blocking findings) yet has not accumulated the required review_clean_rounds/audit clean rounds. Under the default of 2, the first clean round matches no review branch (branch 1 false: not yet converged; branch 2 false: nothing blocking; branch 3 false when no mechanize class) and matches neither audit state (non-converged but zero open non-PASS rows), leaving next_action undefined exactly where an agent needs 'run the next round'. Test 14 only exercises the three named branches, so the gap is untested.
suggestion: Add an explicit terminal/default branch (lowest precedence) for a clean-but-not-yet-converged round on both loops, naming the next-round command (e.g. review: spawn reviewers then 'tp review <spec> --record <file>'; audit: 'tp audit <spec> --record <file>'), and state that non-converged audit covers a clean-but-under-count round too (not only open non-PASS rows). Extend Test 14 to assert next_action for a first-of-N clean round.

finding: §3.4 states the live recompute leaves 'no stored boolean left to go stale', implying new-format --record no longer persists a per-round clean flag. But §4.1 explicitly routes a round where 'no finding carries a severity at all' — a genuinely possible NEW-format round if an LLM reviewer omits the severity field on every row — to the round-level legacy fallback, which §3.4 defines as reading 'its stored clean flag'. The spec never says whether --record under this release must continue writing that stored clean flag, so the fallback for an all-missing-severity new round is undefined: there may be no flag to read.
suggestion: State explicitly whether new-format --record continues to persist a per-round clean flag. Either require it to keep writing the flag (so the §4.1 all-missing-severity fallback is always well-defined), or define the fallback behavior for a new round that carries findings but no severities and no stored flag (e.g. treat as blocking/not-clean under the same conservative rule §4.1 uses per-finding).

finding: The next_action precedence has no branch for the most common mid-loop state: a clean round that has NOT yet reached the required consecutive count (review_clean_rounds/audit_clean_rounds, default 2). For review, such a round is not converged (branch 1 fails), has no convergence-blocking unresolved findings (branch 2 fails), and may have no mechanize_candidates (branch 3 fails) — so all three listed branches skip it and next_action's value is undefined. For audit, §8.2 explicitly asserts 'only two states apply: a converged audit round ... a non-converged audit round (open non-PASS rows)'; a clean audit round with zero non-PASS rows that is still one round short of convergence is neither, disproving the 'only two states' claim. Test 14 therefore cannot assert next_action's expected value for the ordinary 'clean, record the next round' state, so two engineers write contradictory (or no) assertions.
suggestion: Add an explicit fallthrough branch: for a clean-but-not-yet-converged round, next_action names the command to record/run the next review or audit round (e.g. spawn the panel, merge, then `tp review|audit <spec> --record <file>`). State it as the lowest-precedence default so every reachable state maps to exactly one next_action, and update §8.2's audit 'only two states apply' wording to include it.

finding: The review next_action precedence is not a total function over reachable states, despite §8.2 claiming a 'fixed precedence so a state satisfying several conditions is unambiguous' and despite the audit paragraph explicitly enumerating all its states ('only two states apply'). The three review branches are (1) converged, (2) convergence-blocking unresolved findings present, (3) mechanize_candidates present. Under the new 'blocking' default a round whose surviving findings are all medium/low is clean (§3.2, §4.1) but, with review_clean_rounds=2, still needs another consecutive clean round to converge. That state — not converged, no blocking findings, no mechanize_candidates — matches no branch, so next_action names nothing exactly in the common 'run the next review round' case that is the loop's normal progression. This is distinct from the prior 'exactly one command vs three triggers' ambiguity findings, which concern choosing among the listed branches, not a missing branch. Test 14 also exercises only the three enumerated states, never the clean-but-not-yet-converged one.
suggestion: Add an explicit fall-through branch (lowest precedence): a clean-but-not-yet-converged review round names the next-round command (spawn the reviewer panel / run tp review for the next round, then tp review <spec> --record <file>), mirroring the audit paragraph's fix-and-re-audit terminal branch, and add a Test 14 case for it so the precedence is provably total.

finding: next_action branch 2 names --resolve/--resolve-all as the forward step for convergence-blocking findings, but that action contradicts two of the release's own invariants. (a) Because --record rejects 'fixed' rows (§3.5), the only convergence-effective disposition reachable through that command is wontfix/duplicate — i.e. accepting/disposing the blocking finding rather than removing the defect. Advising this as the default next step reintroduces the exact 'make findings disappear' pressure the release exists to remove (Principle 3: altitude 'must be a reviewer saying it, never the orchestrator asserting it to make findings disappear'; §3.1's grind-until-nothing-survives incentive). (b) Disposing a blocking (including critical) finding wontfix is framed elsewhere as 'an explicit, evidenced human acceptance' (§3.5) and a user-approved decision (CLAUDE.md self-development rules), never the agent's own — yet next_action, an advisory the agent reads as its literal next command, nudges the agent to make that acceptance. The canonical response to a blocking finding is to revise the spec and re-review, which branch 2 never names.
suggestion: Make branch 2's default directive 'revise the spec to address the blocking findings, then re-review' and reserve the --resolve/--resolve-all disposition command for operator-driven acceptance (as §4.2/§8.3 describe for non-blocking findings), rather than auto-suggesting disposition of blocking findings — so next_action never steers the agent to dispose a blocking finding on its own.

finding: The new closing sentence of §3.5 adds a normative rule — "`--record` rejects a findings file still carrying `fixed` rows" — but, unlike the other new rejection introduced this release (§6.2 specifies "usage error (exit 2) with a hint"), it names no exit code or hint, and §11 adds no acceptance test exercising a `fixed`-row rejection.
suggestion: State the exit code and hint for the `--record` rejection of `fixed` rows, mirroring §6.2's exit-2-with-hint discipline, and add a §11 acceptance test covering it.

finding: The round-4 rewrite of §8.2 point 1 reframes the converged next_action as a directive/marker rather than a command — for audit, "the terminal marker `converged — implementation verified, proceed to release`, which names no further tp command." But the unchanged final paragraph of §8.2 still calls that same converged-audit state "the forward command (proceed)," and unchanged §8.1 still says next_action names "the single next command." The same value is described both as a command and as naming no command; the command/directive distinction introduced in point 1 was not propagated to §8.1 or §8.2's audit paragraph.
suggestion: Propagate the distinction: reword §8.1 to "the single next step (a runnable tp command or a short directive)" and change §8.2's audit paragraph from "names the forward command (proceed)" to "names the forward step (the terminal proceed marker)."

finding: §8.4 justifies next_action surviving --compact because it 'changes the agent's very next call', then asserts nonblocking_open survives too but gives it no analogous justification. By §4.2 nonblocking_open's job is to make accepted-open 'visible/auditable' — the same audit-only purpose §8.4 uses to strip harness_note/harness_stale from compact as 'unactionable'. nonblocking_open never changes the agent's next call: at convergence next_action deliberately does not push resolve (§8.2), and on a clean-but-not-yet-converged round the next step is 'run the next round' regardless of the count. So an emitted count is retained in the always-on compact path against §8.4's own stated standard.
suggestion: Either strip nonblocking_open under --compact alongside the other audit-visibility diagnostics, or add an explicit rationale in §8.4 for why a non-command count an agent never branches on must survive compaction — the current text retains it without the survival justification it demands of next_action.
